leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2012 Human Rights Report on Central African Republic
leads.documents: Penal code criminalization of 'public expression of love' between persons of same sex, penalties including 6 months to 2 years imprisonment or 150,000-600,000 CFA francs fine, enhanced penalty when child involved, and that there were no reports police arrested or detained persons under these provisions in 2012; also societal discrimination against LGBT persons entrenched and attributed to Western influence.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "U.S. Department of State's 2012 human rights report" and "U.S. Department of State's 2012 Human Rights Report" - no URL visible in text

leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2023 Human Rights Report on Central African Republic
leads.documents: Living conditions for LGBTQ people including religious preaching of conversion rarely enacted because identities kept hidden, and no reports of intersex-normalizing surgeries occurring in 2023.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "The 2023 Human Rights Report" - no URL visible in text

leads.title: Constitution of the Central African Republic, Article 7
leads.documents: Constitutional ban on same-sex marriage; marriage defined as 'the union between one man and one woman' with family and marriage under protection of the State; basis for no legal recognition of same-sex couples.
leads.detail: Cited in text as Article 7 of the Constitution quote - no URL visible in text

leads.title: Law 24-001 on the Protection of Personal Data, Article 17
leads.documents: Protects sexual orientation as sensitive data; prohibits processing of sensitive data due to risks of discrimination or infringement of personal freedoms.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "Law 24-001 on the Protection of Personal Data" Article 17 quote - no URL visible in text

leads.title: Alternatives Centrafrique - Universal Periodic Review fourth cycle report
leads.documents: Local LGBTQ organization founded 2009 registered 2020; documented cases of arrests due to false accusations of same-sex intercourse; mistreatment and torture of LGBTQ people by law enforcement.
leads.detail: Cited in text as Alternatives Centrafrique fourth cycle report for the Universal Periodic Review - no URL visible in text

leads.title: Alternatives Centrafrique - Universal Periodic Review third cycle report
leads.documents: Submission by local LGBTQ organization to UPR rights machinery documenting LGBTQ situation in CAR.
leads.detail: Cited in text as Alternatives Centrafrique submitted reports for the Universal Periodic Review's third and fourth cycle - no URL visible in text

leads.title: United Nations joint statement on ending acts of violence and related human rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity
leads.documents: CAR as one of few African states signing joint statement condemning violence and discrimination against LGBTQ people.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'joint statement on ending acts of violence and related human rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity' at the United Nations - no URL visible in text

leads.title: Central African Republic National HIV Plan 2016 to 2020 / Global Fund Project
leads.documents: Recognized men who have sex with men as a key population for focus; context for HIV-related workplace stigmatization, harassment, blackmail and firings.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "country's National HIV Plan from 2016 to 2020" for Global Fund Project - no URL visible in text

leads.title: U.S. Department of State reporting on LGBTQ organizations in CAR
leads.documents: States there were no LGBTQ organizations within the country, contrasting with Alternatives Centrafrique claim of existence since 2009/registration 2020.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "According to the U.S Department of State, there were no LGBTQ organizations within the country" - no URL visible in text
